chunks: Ahmad narrated from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot to lie on his right side after the two rak'ahs of Fajr prayer, and remembered when the call to prayer (Iqamah) had begun. He said: 'He performs the Iqamah and prays, and leaves that (the missed position) aside, and there is no harm in that.'

key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: The Iqamah (the second, shorter call to prayer immediately preceding the start of salat)
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: The two rak'ahs of the Fajr (dawn) prayer
key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible (indicating an excusable omission)
key_terms.يَضْطَجِعَ عَلَى يَمِينِهِ: To lie on the right side (a recommended sunnah posture after the first two rak'ahs)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they forget to lie on their right side after the first two rak'ahs of Fajr prayer and remember during the Iqamah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) addresses the fiqh of *nasī* (forgetfulness) regarding the recommended posture of lying on the right side after the two rak'ahs of Fajr. The Imam’s ruling that one should simply proceed with the Iqamah and prayer without reversion highlights the Shia principle of ease (*yusr*) in ritual acts, distinguishing between obligatory pillars and recommended sunan where omission does not invalidate the prayer.
